description:
The US has not disabled Iran’s military capabilities, Wolfgang Pusztai, former Austrian defence attache to Libya, tells Al Jazeera.

“For the time being, neither side has an intention to escalate,” Pusztai said.

Tehran or Washington could be forced to escalate, however, if either side endures further civilian or military casualties, the defence analyst said.

Iran appears unwilling to escalate as Tehran could have struck additional targets and American bases in the region but refrained from doing so, he said. The US also appears unwilling as Washington did not use short- and medium-range ballistic missiles in their strikes this week, the former defence attache argued.

“I’m rather optimistic that we will not see a major escalation in the near future”, Pusztai remarked, saying that he would advise Tehran to take a “peaceful approach” to living with its Gulf neighbours and not “threaten them every other day” with missiles.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, created in 1975 after the Arab oil embargo, currently holds around 290 million barrels, less than half of its 700-million-barrel capacity and its lowest level since 1983. Stored in 61 salt caverns along the Gulf Coast, the reserve was significantly drawn down following the Russia-Ukraine war and this year’s Strait of Hormuz closure. A recent Government Accountability Office report warned that ageing infrastructure could hinder future emergency releases, with about a quarter of the reserve currently unavailable for drawdown. The Energy Department has allocated $1.4 billion for repairs, but officials say full restoration could take up to seven years.

Al Jazeera’s Eva McKend reports from Washington, DC.

description:
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright has visited Caracas to sign major oil agreements with the Venezuelan government as Washington seeks a greater role in the country’s energy sector.

The agreements are described as giving US interests control over a significant share of Venezuela’s oil reserves and increasing US involvement in 17 oil fields.

Supporters say the deals could help stabilise oil supplies and prices while reducing the role of Chinese and Russian companies in Venezuela’s energy industry.

Venezuelan Interim President Delcy Rodriguez described the agreements as historic.

But the deals have also raised questions over Venezuelan sovereignty, US interests and who will ultimately benefit from the country’s vast oil resources.

The report examines the political and economic implications of the agreements and the changing balance of influence over Venezuela’s oil industry.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Iranian local reports and state media have confirmed that civilians, including children, were killed in US strikes near Sirik in southern Iran overnight on September 1-2,, with Tehran condemning the attack as a war crime. Researcher Ali Akbar Dareini of the Centre for Strategic Studies in Tehran told Al Jazeera that the attack "cannot be ignored" and that Iran has to respond. He said this is "a prelude to a bigger war", arguing that the US is combining sanctions, a naval blockade and military strikes in the hope of forcing Iran to surrender. Dareini said Iran finds it necessary to "escalate and raise the costs of war for Trump", adding that this is "the only viable option" for Iran at this point. He said Iran remains in firm control of the Strait of Hormuz, but that the strait will remain closed as long as the US military campaign continues. He stated: "If Iran cannot export oil or cannot import materials, no one in this region will do so."

title: Iran warns US confrontation could be ‘a prelude to a bigger war’: Analysis

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
In Buenos Aires, Argentina, tango is being used as a therapeutic tool for people living with Parkinson’s disease.

The programme combines dance and movement exercises to help patients work on balance, walking and other motor skills, while also providing emotional and social support.

Patient Jorge Alberto Alvarez describes how tango helps him manage symptoms including tremors and rigidity.

At Ramos Mejia Hospital, neurologist Dr Tomoko Arakaki discusses research into how dance and movement may support the brain’s ability to adapt and develop new neural pathways.

Instructor Laura Segade guides participants through exercises designed to improve movement and confidence.

For new student Julio, the experience becomes an emotional breakthrough, highlighting how movement and music can offer another way of living with Parkinson’s.
